findings: Queries cover dates within the past 30 days, with at most 10000 rows per query.
Changes can take up to three minutes to appear.
Not every account change has a corresponding ChangeEvent.
Google Ads Editor changes are unsupported in ChangeEvent despite the client enum value.
Detailed old/new fields identify recorded changes, not absence of every possible intervening writer.
Queries cover dates within the past 90 days, with at most 10000 rows per query.
Changes can take up to three minutes to appear.
Only the latest change for a resource within the queried window is returned.
A parent resource change can represent subordinate activity, not a specific campaign status transition.
Not every ChangeStatus row has detailed ChangeEvent fields.

provider_history_limits.assessment_inference: Combining these reports can expose changes but does not prove the absence of an intervening activation or owner stop immediately before a later dispatch. Neither an empty report nor the latest local pause establishes never-launched history or exclusion of concurrent external writers.
prohibited_substitutes: Absence of a local execution ledger entry.
Current PAUSED plus original PAUSED creation.
Latest Mezan pause or naming/label resemblance.
A waiting period alone; it does not prevent a new external change after the wait.
provider_history_limits.operational_blocker: No reviewed enforceable provider/operational exclusion contract establishes uninterrupted launch/stop provenance. Automatic first-funded launch remains withheld.

existing_reuse: One common transaction reads guard and both policies; owner policy revision races are serialized.
Standing commitments count current enabled inventory and unreflected pending positive increments once.
The hardened commit path makes one commit attempt and preserves ambiguous reservations/fences.
Recovery observation does not confer dispatch authority or release uncertain budget.
gaps: LaunchAllocation is a storage command; it does not independently prove fresh product/native intent, owner activation/caps/auth_epoch, or original creation/fence identity.
BudgetGuardSnapshot has guard and policy rows, but no same-session original intent, completed proposal, native operation fence or authentication epoch dependency.
The synchronous planner cannot independently load those source rows within the transaction.
StandingBudgetReservation requires standing management activation and policy/claim digest. Fabricating such a policy or enable claim for first launch would conflate two distinct authorizations.
A dedicated launch authority module cannot safely compensate for absent shared-guard transaction inputs outside that transaction.
future_interface_owned_by_shared_guard_m: A typed launch reservation command that binds exact owner revision, activation generation, auth_epoch, expiry, immutable creation identity, completed proposal, operation fence and independently trusted provenance.
Same-session reads/CAS dependencies for all mutable authority rows; fresh native semantic evidence remains timestamped outside the transaction and rechecked at the dispatch boundary.
Refactor/reuse the common commitment calculation for existing unshared budget identity and only its incremental unreflected commitment; never reserve the same current or pending amount twice.
Explicit ambiguous claim/commit states keep the reservation/fence and prohibit resubmission until independent settlement proves the result.
Revocation must remain available without OAuth; transaction failure must never fall back to non-atomic writes.
tests_required_if_positive_interface_bec: Actual replica-set races for owner revoke/revision/auth_epoch and simultaneous standing increases/launch reservations.
Unknown commit or provider acknowledgement cannot release, retry, or duplicate budget.
Existing budget reflected in current inventory and matching pending claim are counted once.
Manual campaigns, unknown provenance, intervening external changes and owner-stop evidence cannot be adopted.

catalog_boundaries: Current native owner-selected product_id/merchant_id/offer_id mapping is not independent section-membership evidence or a cross-platform identity graph.
Current product lookup includes feed_label, but selected-offer eligibility is compared by offer_id; distinct feed/language identities must not be assumed equivalent.
Proven section membership, stable native catalog identities, hidden/unavailable exclusions and product landing URLs belong to the separate seasons/catalog bridge work.
A product performing well on another platform is a test candidate, not proof of Google performance; orders/platform conversions and currencies must remain separately attributed.
honest_owner_flow: Save reviewable season/market/products/section/audience/exclusions and explicit financial bounds; natural-language recommendations alone confer no spending authority.
Show verified product and inventory evidence, missing costs, native prerequisites and campaign-type coverage before making a claim of readiness.
Where deployed executors and valid owner policy permit it, prepare/create supported Search/RSA campaigns as PAUSED. This assessment does not enable that policy.
After creation, reread the selected campaign/product/native settings and present the exact per-campaign preview with account currency, budget semantics and material risks.

When uninterrupted stop history cannot be established, require a fresh explicit owner instruction for that specific manual enable proposal. Reuse the existing manual native gateway; do not disguise standing automation as manual approval.

Changed or expired preview, revoked owner, missing approved limits, unknown dispatch/acknowledgement or failed freshness prevents a new dispatch. Retain ambiguous reservations/fences and reconcile without resending.
Report verified native result or uncertainty; a human approval is a new instruction, not retrospective proof of never-launched history or an external-writer lock.
Keep automatic first-funded launch and automatic resume withheld until their separate provenance and authority contracts are established.
